claims.statement: compose.yaml defines 18 services: 8 built app images (app, idp, note-service, tags-service, todo-service, feedback-service, meal-service, focus-service), 8 per-service Redis instances, postgres-feedback and rabbitmq-feedback.
The monorepo holds nine apps and ten packages; the app-side Next.js server is the only API caller to domain services.

Two hard contracts bind the apps: shared UI rendered from @life/ui (no raw visual HTML in app code) and the BE → cache → DB layering; requests reach the app through a Tailscale access gate before any of it.

scripts/arch-check.mjs mechanically enforces five topology rules: one database per service (RULE 3), designated engine with feedback-service allowlisted for Postgres (RULE 4), no cross-service store access, diff-scoped (RULE 5), required env forwarded to each service's compose environment block (RULE 6), and no self-hosted runners in workflows (RULE 7).
Rules 3, 4 and 6 judge the resulting topology (compose + sources on disk), never the diff; rules 5 and 7 are diff-scoped or workflow-scoped respectively.
Every non-feedback service is SQLite with one database file per service on a bind-mounted data directory; feedback-service is the only Postgres service.
